title: European Baking Traditions
description: Centuries-old techniques — laminated doughs, precise sponge work, and layered tortes — passed down through generations of home and professional bakers across the continent. Many of these cakes are tied to specific regional pastry guilds and royal courts, with recipes that have barely changed in over a century.
specialty: Structured, technique-driven layer cakes and pastries

title: Asia & Middle East Baking Traditions
description: A wide range of baking styles shaped by local staples — rice flour, coconut, semolina, and rosewater-scented syrups — often steamed or baked in ways that prioritize delicate texture over heavy richness. Many recipes are built around celebrating specific festivals or life milestones.
specialty: Delicate, aromatic cakes built on regional staple ingredients

title: Latin American Baking Traditions
description: A tradition built on milk-soaked sponges, dulce de leche, and tropical fruit, blending Indigenous, European, and African culinary influences into cakes designed to be shared at large family gatherings.

title: North American Baking Traditions
description: A tradition shaped by 20th-century home-baking culture — boxed mixes, potluck classics, and bold, generous flavors — alongside regional specialties tied to specific cities and immigrant communities.
specialty: Bold, generously frosted layer cakes and bundt classics
